name: Green anarchism
summary: Green anarchism combines the anarchist rejection of the state and hierarchy with an ecological critique, holding that states, capitalism and industrial production drive environmental destruction. It favours stateless, decentralised, bioregional or communal societies, degrowth, direct action and, in some strands, animal liberation. Strands divide mainly over technology and civilization: primitivists want to abandon agriculture and industry, while social ecologists keep reason, cities and technology under democratic control.
scope: Green anarchism (eco-anarchism): the anarchist school that ties environmental crisis to hierarchy, state and capitalism, as Gordon (s5), Price (s6) and EBSCO (s7) define it. It names three main tendencies: Bookchin's social ecology, Næss-style deep ecology (as taken up by Earth First!) and Zerzan's anarcho-primitivism, with Fifth Estate, Green Anarchy and Green Anarchist as its periodicals; the classical roots are Kropotkin and Reclus. Where tendencies disagree (foraging, population, technology, electoral municipal politics) the answer is a split or null. Excluded: Bookchin's later communalism where it breaks with anarchism, Kaczynski and violent offshoots, and eco-socialism or green politics in general. Wikipedia only guided the search.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Price says Zerzan makes the division of labor the core of the problem and wants society before it; Bookchin lists rotation of work and says no national division of labor is needed (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction and 'Toward a Liberatory Technology', p. 159).

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Bookchin wants to eliminate the money economy and do away with commodity relations (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'Toward a Liberatory Technology', p. 159; Introduction, p. 21).

all-land-state-owned.rationale: Bookchin, Post-Scarcity Anarchism (footnote in title essay) calls the socialist retention of state and 'nationalized' property reactionary, and Ecology of Freedom (ch. 2-3 on primitive communism) says public or nationalized property keeps proprietorship alive.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The IFA principles summarised in the EBSCO overview (s7) list humane treatment of animals as a core green-anarchist principle, which presupposes that animal suffering matters; sentience itself is not discussed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: EBSCO (s7) reports the IFA principle endorsing humane treatment of animals used for food, which accepts food use under humane conditions; anti-civilisation writers on hunting and other strands are not shown to differ.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Post-Scarcity Anarchism (Introduction and title essay) says cybernated machinery can reduce toil to near vanishing and gives freedom from toil as the basis of a free society; this is Bookchin's strand, and the anti-technology strand is not shown stating a position on it.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Price says Bookchin found hierarchy and domination more pernicious and ingrained than economic class, and Bookchin says hierarchy goes beyond the Marxian class definition (Ecology of Freedom, opening discussion of hierarchy); Zerzan instead stresses division of labor and symbolic culture as the root.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Kropotkin's Mutual Aid (introduction and conclusion) argues mutual aid, not mutual struggle, is the dominant factor of progress and that even success in war tracks the mutual aid within each side.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Bookchin in Post-Scarcity Anarchism (the 'consumer society' passages, ch. 'Towards a Liberatory Technology' era essays) and Ecology of Freedom ch. 3 call consumerism mindless, contrived and a plunder of the human spirit and the earth.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Gordon says the anarchist emphasis on decentralisation and worker/community ownership leads to visions of communistic localism and bio-regionalism, and Bookchin calls for small, balanced, decentralised ecocommunities (Post-Scarcity Anarchism). Mainly the social-ecology and eco-anarchist strands.

decide-locally.rationale: Gordon names decentralization and communistic localism or bioregionalism as the eco-anarchist outlook, Price describes Bookchin's face-to-face municipal assemblies confederated upward, and Bookchin wants small decentralized communes (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, pp. 62-63); the primitivist strand also wants small bands.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Price presents Bookchin's green anarchist politics as opposing representative democracy and statecraft in favour of face-to-face assemblies, and Post-Scarcity Anarchism rejects electoral and parliamentary politics as the opposite of libertarian politics.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bookchin says a revolutionary group aims at dissolving power rather than seizing it, and attacks the state form as such (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'Ecology and Revolutionary Thought', p. 70), which excludes dictatorial rule by any class.

direct-action.rationale: Bookchin calls direct action a basic revolutionary strategy for abolishing the state without state institutions (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction, p. 22), and Gordon and Price describe direct action as the main practice of eco-anarchism.

direct-votes.rationale: Price reports that Bookchin's social ecology rests on face-to-face, directly democratic assemblies, and Bookchin calls the assembly the authentic basis of democracy (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction); this is the social-ecology strand, the primitivist strand states no such rule.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Bookchin states that an anarchist or anarcho-communist society presupposes distribution of goods according to individual needs and presents this as the anatomy of the free society he advocates (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction, p. 21).

domination-women-nature.rationale: Gordon presents eco-feminism within eco-anarchism as stressing an inexorable link between dominating nature and dominating humans, with patriarchy as the prototype of both; Zerzan (Future Primitive) likewise ties social domination to domination of nature.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Bookchin (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, introduction) treats counterculture experiments in communal living, sexual freedom and dress as the latently revolutionary seeds of a free society.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: EBSCO says green anarchism is set apart by its rejection of enforced environmentalism and other authoritarian social control, which counts against letting environmental goals override liberty by compulsion.

equal-outcomes.rationale: EBSCO reports the Eco-anarchist Manifesto affirming the economic equality of all people; Bookchin's own rule is distribution by need, so this is a thin match to 'equality of outcomes'.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Bookchin retracts his earlier inclusion of nuclear fuels in an energy mix as cutting across the entire grain of his thinking (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction); Gordon describes anti-nuclear mobilization as a founding site of eco-anarchist direct action.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Bookchin refuses to give utopian blueprints and leaves to each community, and to future generations, the choice of how to organise production (Ecology of Freedom, 'An Ecological Society', p. 345); Zerzan likewise holds that defining a disalienated world would be impossible and undesirable (Future Primitive, final section).

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Bookchin (Ecology of Freedom, Introduction) argues that command-and-obedience hierarchy perpetuates unfreedom even without economic exploitation or political coercion.

future-generations.rationale: The EBSCO overview lists as one of green anarchism's six core principles that each generation must leave the environment in better condition than it found it.

gm-crops.rationale: The EBSCO summary of the Green Anarchist International Association's principles says green anarchists are wary of genetically oriented research because its applications could threaten liberty; wariness rather than a flat ban, so not -2.

gradual-change.rationale: Bookchin argues the ecological contradiction cannot be redeemed by reforms, concessions or modifications of strategy (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'Ecology and Revolutionary Thought', p. 61); Price's account of his assembly-building is more incremental, so not a strong -2.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Ecology of Freedom (ch. on organic society) describes resources as belonging to the user only while used, with usufruct overriding proprietorship, which is at odds with lasting title gained by first use; this is presented mainly as a feature of organic societies.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Zerzan (Future Primitive, final section) says agriculture and symbolic culture were a monstrously wrong turn that lowered the quality of human life and ended a 'state of grace'; this is the anti-civilisation strand, and no social-ecology source states the opposite.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Gordon describes eco-anarchist and eco-feminist activism as connecting militarism, poverty and environmental destruction as manifestations of one patriarchal contempt for life, a critique of domination as such.

keep-public-institutions-small.rationale: Price describes Bookchin's call for face-to-face assemblies in the smallest local municipality, and Ecology of Freedom (ch. 5 on delegated power) says power beyond localized areas loses its human scale; social-ecology strand.

local-production.rationale: Kropotkin's Fields, Factories and Workshops (ch. 1) argues each nation should be its own agriculturist and manufacturer, and Bookchin (Ecology of Freedom, intro) wants local resources worked by decentralised communities; the Ecoanarchist Manifesto as reported in s7 says self-sufficiency is not a primary principle.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Social ecology (Ecology of Freedom ch. 1, Post-Scarcity Anarchism) rejects economic determinism and says hierarchy goes beyond and precedes class; Zerzan's primitivism (s2) likewise traces civilisation to symbolic culture and domestication rather than the economy alone.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bookchin says the revolutionary group's theory must be its practice and must be organized on the decentralizing principles of the society it seeks (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'Ecology and Revolutionary Thought', p. 70); EBSCO adds that green anarchists reject authoritarian means.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: Bookchin, Post-Scarcity Anarchism (title essay pp. 69-71): the revolutionary group is a catalyst not a 'vanguard', and power problems can only be solved if there is no above or below, which excludes military-style command.

municipal-property.rationale: Gordon says anarchist emphasis on worker/community ownership coheres with a low-throughput economy and leads to communistic localism; he does not spell out exclusion of both private and national-state ownership.

national-self-determination.rationale: Ward (ch. 4 and the chapter on federalism) presents anarchists as opposing nation states, preferring federalism, and treating nationalist movements as prone to extremism; a state for every nation is not endorsed.

natural-rulers.rationale: The EBSCO entry gives opposition to all social and political hierarchy as a defining principle, and Bookchin traces domination to hierarchy itself (Ecology of Freedom), which a class of born rulers would contradict.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: EBSCO says green anarchism's mandate extends to plant and animal kingdoms and that humans have no innate right to jurisdiction over nature, and Price describes Naess's intrinsic value as one strand; Bookchin's social ecology does not state it that way.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Green anarchism as described by EBSCO and Gordon seeks a society without formal government, so government existing even for protection alone contradicts the stated goal.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: Bookchin, Post-Scarcity Anarchism (title essay, p. 61): post-scarcity removes any need for 'transitional' stages or centralized organizations between the present and the free society.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bookchin says a revolutionary group is a catalyst and not a vanguard, aiming at the dissolution rather than the seizure of power (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'Ecology and Revolutionary Thought', p. 70), and the sources call for abolishing the state, so a ruling party is excluded.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Bookchin (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 2nd-ed. introduction) sets libertarian politics against parliamentary politics, party organization and electoral mobilization; Price (green anarchism) describes the same rejection of representative democracy and the state. They reject it as antithetical rather than weighing its viability.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Bookchin's social-ecology strand states that representation should give way to face-to-face general assemblies of free individuals (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'Ecology and Revolutionary Thought'), and Price's account presents the same directly democratic municipal politics. Stated from the social-ecology strand; the anti-civilisation strand does not contradict it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Bookchin (Ecology of Freedom, Introduction) names the domination of women by men as a core hierarchy, and Gordon says eco-anarchists treat patriarchy as the prototype of domination.

pay-for-effort.rationale: Bookchin, Ecology of Freedom (ch. 6, irreducible minimum) holds that the means of life should be assured irrespective of productive contribution and distributed by need, and calls the shift to rewards a subversion of freedom; social-ecology strand only.

people-in-arms.rationale: Bookchin (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'The Forms of Freedom') wants social weight shifted to 'the armed people in permanent assembly', and Ecology of Freedom laments citizen militias being replaced by professional armies; stated only in passing.

physical-labour-duty.rationale: Kropotkin, Fields, Factories and Workshops (ch. 8 and the integrated-labour passage): each able-bodied person should be a worker combining manual and intellectual work, and each healthy man and woman should spend part of life in manual work.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: Bookchin, Ecology of Freedom (ch. 12 on the assembly) calls quorums and consensus degrading to real democracy; the anti-civ side (Zerzan) only describes foragers deciding by consensus without stating it as a method.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: The defining sources diverge: EBSCO says green anarchism rejects ecoterrorism as authoritarian, while Price says primitivists and deep ecologists back attacks on technology 'often through violent means'.

positive-liberty.rationale: Bookchin's central post-scarcity thesis is that freedom depends on a technology of abundance, and he says choice presupposes a sufficiency in the means of life (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction; Ecology of Freedom, discussion of scarcity and need).

power-shapes-accepted-knowledge.rationale: Price and Bookchin (Ecology of Freedom) describe an 'epistemology of rule' in which hierarchical power shapes the mindset that presents domination as natural.

production-for-use.rationale: Bookchin contrasts a society organized around satisfying human needs with 'production for the sake of production' under capitalism (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction), and wants an economy freed from the money economy (p. 159).

property-fundamental.rationale: Bookchin lists the abolition of private property as a precondition of the anarchist society he describes (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction, p. 21), and Zerzan presents foragers as having no concept of private property (Future Primitive, final section); the EBSCO entry adds only that green anarchism wants wealth in common hands, not that owners' rights be protected.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The EBSCO overview says green anarchism does not outright oppose private property but wants such systems to put wealth in the hands of the common people rather than a controlling elite.

recall-officials.rationale: Bookchin (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'The Forms of Freedom') says committee members must be subject to immediate recall by the assembly, and Ecology of Freedom praises libertarian confederations with recallable elected chiefs.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Price and Gordon say primitivists like Zerzan call for a return to small gatherer-hunter life, while Bookchin says he does not mean that we must return to the primitive lifeways of our early ancestors (Ecology of Freedom, final chapter 'An Ecological Society').

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Revolution is the central method in Bookchin's key work, which says either revolution creates an ecological society or humanity and nature are lost (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction, p. 24), and Gordon speaks of primitivism within 'anarchist revolutionary struggles'.

simple-living.rationale: EBSCO calls a simple, sustainable lifestyle a core idea of contemporary green anarchism, whereas Bookchin in Ecology of Freedom (final chapter, on utopian traditions) criticises the 'voluntary simplicity' of the counterculture as denying the need for physical and cultural complexity.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Bookchin (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, title essay) says the revolutionary goal is the dissolution of power, not respect for existing institutions; only a single strand speaks to this.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Price presents Bookchin's social ecology, his example of green anarchism, as aiming to oppose and replace the nation state with confederated assemblies; Ecology of Freedom (ch. 'An Ecological Society') speaks of dissolving State power.

state-harmful.rationale: Bookchin calls the absolute negation of the state anarchism (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'Ecology and Revolutionary Thought', p. 63), Price says his aim is to oppose and replace the nation state, and EBSCO defines the ideology as abolishing formal government.

strong-leader.rationale: The EBSCO entry gives opposition to all forms of political hierarchy and to centralized authority as green anarchism's key principle, which a leader empowered to override institutions would contradict; Bookchin likewise aims at dissolving power (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'The Forms of Freedom').

technology-design-reflects-political-int.rationale: Ecology of Freedom (p. 290, on technics) rejects the view that technology is value-free and distinguishes libertarian from authoritarian technics, with centralised industrial technology tied to hierarchy.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Ward's anarchism introduction (ch. 4) describes anarchists as having absolute hostility to territorial politics and a direct rejection of imperialism, which excludes expansion by a strong nation.

total-state.rationale: The sources call for abolishing the state and oppose all centralized authority (EBSCO; Price on Bookchin; Post-Scarcity Anarchism, p. 63), so a state directing every area of life is the opposite.

traditional-family.rationale: Bookchin says the patriarchal and nuclear family planted the seed of domination and that monogamy and patriarchy lose their rationale in a post-scarcity society (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, Introduction); Zerzan contrasts forager child-rearing favorably with 'isolated nuclear families' (Future Primitive).

unions-run-economy.rationale: Bookchin, Ecology of Freedom (closing chapters) criticizes 'hierarchical syndicalism' and the pyramidal structure of syndicalist theory; Post-Scarcity Anarchism says unions, like parties, tend to become ends in themselves. Price only cites a green-syndicalist book in a note.

vanguard-party.rationale: Bookchin (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, passage on the revolutionary group) says a revolutionary group should see itself as a catalyst, not a 'vanguard', and aim to dissolve power rather than seize it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: EBSCO, citing the Ecoanarchist Manifesto, says green anarchists reject capitalism as 'rule by the rich' and want wealth in common hands, not in an elite that uses it to maintain social control.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Bookchin, Post-Scarcity Anarchism (title essay p. 69; 'Towards a Liberatory Technology' pp. 115-116) treats the left's work ethic as an obstacle to revolution and welcomes a toil-less way of life; this is the social-ecology strand, Zerzan (Future Primitive) praises foragers' little work.

worker-ownership.rationale: Gordon says the anarchist emphasis on decentralization and worker/community ownership fits a low-throughput economy; Bookchin separately says workers' management alone is not enough and puts control in community assemblies (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'The Forms of Freedom').

workers-councils.rationale: Bookchin accepts factory committees as a means of taking over the economy but says councils are class structures that cannot be the final form, and puts the community assembly at the basis of democracy (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'The Forms of Freedom' and Introduction).

workers-nation.rationale: Bookchin (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, preface) calls revolution at home the highest act of internationalism and solidarity with oppressed people abroad, which cuts against putting national solidarity first.

workers-own-party.rationale: Post-Scarcity Anarchism (Introduction, p. 50) says libertarian visions of politics have as their antithesis parliamentary politics, party organisation and electoral mobilisation, which excludes a party of working people.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: Bookchin (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 2nd-ed. introduction) names party organization and electoral mobilization as the antithesis of libertarian politics; he does not address reform campaigns by workers' parties as such.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Gordon notes the anarchist emphasis on worker and community ownership, and Bookchin (Post-Scarcity Anarchism, 'The Forms of Freedom') wants factory committees run directly by workers' assemblies, though he warns that worker management alone stays a class form.

missingStatements.text: Humanity should abandon agriculture and return to a hunter-gatherer way of life.
missingStatements.rationale: Anarcho-primitivists name agriculture as the origin of hierarchy and want it dissolved, though Bookchin's wing rejects this.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by return-to-foraging, which this audit answers 0 because anarcho-primitivists want agriculture abandoned but Bookchin-style social ecologists reject it.

missingStatements.text: Illegal sabotage of machinery and infrastructure is justified to protect wild nature.
missingStatements.rationale: Earth First! monkeywrenching and ELF actions against deforestation, roadbuilding and pipelines are central to the movement's direct-action tradition.

missingStatements.text: Large areas of land should be returned to wilderness and left free of human management.
missingStatements.rationale: Rewilding is part of primitivist practice and deep ecology's biocentrism in green anarchism.

notes: Searched the defining sources, Bookchin's Post-Scarcity Anarchism and Ecology of Freedom, Kropotkin's Mutual Aid and Fields, Factories and Workshops, Zerzan's Future Primitive and Reclus for every statement; most statements are unanswered because none of these states a position. The main internal split is primitivism versus Bookchin's social ecology (foraging, technology, violence); two 0 answers record it.

keyFigures.role: Anarchist geographer; early ecological and total-liberation thinker
keyFigures.quote: Along with Thoreau, writers and intellectuals, including Élisée Reclus and Leo Tolstoy, contributed to the rise of a movement known as anarcho-naturism
